top_choice_rationale: P002 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) credits one explanatory account of how labour demand responds to technology and trade. Katz anchors the older, well-confirmed evidence on skill supply, skill demand and the wage structure. Autor links the polarisation and task evidence to the trade strand. Hanson, with Autor and Dorn, supplies the transparent quasi-experimental evidence on large, persistent local adjustment costs. The work is mature, with foundational papers from the early 1990s and more than a decade of replication and challenge. The debate concerns magnitudes and shift-share inference, not whether the costs exist. The 2023 and 2024 prizes overlap thematically but not in the object credited, as the round-2 descriptions of those prizes indicate. The citation should say 'empirical analyses' and claim no task or directed-technology theory, which would belong to Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo. Excluding Dorn is a real cost of the three-name cap and should be stated openly. I rank P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) second because it is an equally mature and coherent attribution of the same achievement, and I would vote for it over a split outcome. P003 (Melitz, Helpman) is third: it is a compact, mature discovery with the cleanest pair of names, but it carries uncredited priority claims (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum) and a contested size of welfare gains. P004 is a credible methods contribution with a clean BLP core, but it is narrower in changed understanding and leaves Bresnahan's claim unresolved. I rank it above no award, which is last.
recusal_note: No co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Katz, Hanson, Dorn, Melitz, Helpman, Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent from the profile. My capital-skill complementarity work (with Ohanian, Ríos-Rull and Violante) is in the same literature on technology and wage inequality as P001 and P002, which may incline me toward the skill-premium strand. I have co-authored with Timo Boppart and with John Hassler, the chair, neither of whom is a proposed laureate. This is disclosed and not adjudicated, and I claim no independent verification.
